_comment: Synthetic example - a health insurer's claims anomaly & fraud scoring. NOT high-risk under the AI Act (claims control is not 'risk assessment and pricing', Annex III-5(c)), yet it profiles insured persons: GDPR Art. 22, the EIOPA Opinion (Aug 2025) via DNB and the ZN code of conduct still apply. Shows the 'minimal risk but heavy governance' case and the DORA hook via a vendor dataset.
sys_owner: Example Health Insurer N.V. — Claims Operations
sys_description: A gradient-boosting model that scores incoming care-provider claims and insured-person claim patterns for anomalies (billing errors, upcoding, possible fraud) and routes high scores to a human claims investigator.
intended_purpose: Prioritise claims for manual control before payment. The model never rejects a claim; investigators decide.
data_sources: Claims data warehouse (basic and supplementary package, separated), care-provider register, external fraud-indicator list (licensed).
human_oversight: Every flagged claim is reviewed by a claims investigator who records the decision and reason; unflagged claims follow the normal payment flow. Monthly sample of unflagged claims is reviewed to detect missed cases.

dg_datasets.name: Claims 2019-2025 (basic package)
dg_datasets.purpose: Anomaly features; NOT used for supplementary-package acceptance (ZN code)

dg_lineage: Claims DWH (basic | supplementary, separated at source) + provider register + fraud indicators -> feature store (steward) -> train_v24 / val_v24 -> DeclaratieCheck v2.4 -> anomaly score -> investigator queue -> decision + reason
dg_q_evidence: DQ dashboard 2026-08: completeness 99.2%, duplicates 0.03%; representativeness reviewed per region and provider type, no metric yet (FAIR-2026-05 planned).

gov_literacy.training: Reading anomaly scores; confirmation-bias briefing; how to record an override
Art. 10 data governance; ZN separation of basic/supplementary data
